documented_download_steps: Open the Download Data tab in the Monthly Reported Crime Statistics report
Open or Save As the file
source_contract_findings.documented_update_cadence: each year is updated monthly to account for updates on prior cases
geometry_semantics: Address is provided only to the 100-block level
Address-based incidents are mapped to the block midpoint
Intersection incidents are mapped to the intersection centroid
Sensitive cases may omit case number and specific location information entirely
notes: Portland publicly exposes reported-crime downloads through the PPB open-data page and a dedicated Tableau Download Data tab rather than only image dashboards.
The yearly export contract is now validated against a live downloadable yearly file, not just documentation.
The live yearly export carries offense/date fields sufficient for seven-offense reported-year aggregation from the yearly CSV itself.
The public spatial contract is generalized to block midpoint or intersection centroid and is selectively suppressed for sensitive offenses.
That makes Portland usable for public annual counts and likely control-style reconciliation, but not offense-selective city-share promotion under the repo's current spatial doctrine.
The validated yearly CSV exposes direct offense types and date fields for all seven repo offense families, so reported-year count aggregation is feasible from the public export.
The documented taxonomy is richer than a single category field because it includes OffenseType, OffenseCategory, CrimeAgainst, Custom Crime Category, and OffenseCount.
The blocker is not offense/date availability anymore; it is that the public geometry is generalized and selectively absent, which breaks offense-selective within-city share truth.

sources: PPB Monthly Reported Crime Statistics / NIBRS Statistics dashboard
notes: The validated yearly CSV appears sufficient to build seven-offense reported-year feed totals by ReportDate or ReportMonthYear.
The public NIBRS Statistics dashboard is the stronger public standards-aligned annual anchor for seven-offense reconciliation.
The 2024 annual report is useful context but is not a clean seven-offense anchor by itself because its public narrative uses broader custom groupings in key places.
Those public annual surfaces would still be plausible local_publication annual control anchors if the public geometry remains too coarse for city-share use.

why_not_ready: The public export generalizes locations to 100-block addresses and block-midpoint or intersection-centroid points rather than precise incident points.
The public contract selectively suppresses geometry for sensitive offenses; in the observed live yearly export rape has no public location fields and aggravated assault has heavy public geocode loss.
The packet therefore fails the repo's offense-selective city-share truth requirements even though the yearly count surface is usable.
minimum_change_to_unblock: A more precise or less suppressed incident surface would be required for city-share promotion; more packet work on the current public export alone does not fix the geometry censoring.
If the city-share bar is relaxed for a different product tier, decide explicitly whether generalized block-level geometry and offense-selective suppression are acceptable there.
For count or control use, extract the seven-offense reported-year totals from the yearly CSV and reconcile them to the standards-aligned public dashboard anchor.
